justification: Cap to Medium is correct and empirically grounded. (a) Parked principal IS withdrawable during the bounce: the temp staker holds the 9 positions in Active, strategyless, unpaused pools (side-effects: paused.tempStaker=false, balDOLA/balUSDC == totalStaked exactly); withdraw (L310) and emergencyWithdraw (L355) require only poolState==Active, depositFor credits into an Active pool, and withdrawDisabled returns false when no strategy is set. Parked funds are NOT frozen. (b) The funds at risk live in the TEMP staker, not the original pools, so the original pools' terminal-Migrating state does not trap them; recovery is owner-feasible by redeploying the two V2 strategies with convertToAssets (reset non-idempotency and one-shot finalizeAndReset complicate the runbook but do not lock principal). (c) The YS-02 ordering means a cold real run fails safe at leg1-skim (unauthorized withdrawer) with ZERO funds parked; parking is reachable only AFTER the operator manually grants the withdrawer, so the parked-funds state is gated behind a privileged manual fix with no unprivileged actor. This is protocol-availability/function impact (the committed remediation is dead-on-arrival, the live DOLA-withdraw outage persists, migration cannot complete) with conditional reachability and full owner recovery, no direct theft and no permanent loss. C4 Medium, not High (no no-hypotheticals asset-loss path; funds stay withdrawable) and not Low (deterministic break of the committed fix plus a real mid-migration parked-funds halt — beyond mere spec/state).

The dangling-minter consequence elevates this above a pure post-condition cosmetic; combined with the deterministic-revert-on-correct-state it meets the Medium function/operational-integrity bar. Not Low. (If the minter authorization were already independently scoped/limited, this would be a Low; on the evidence here the standing mint authority justifies Medium.)
